urn:eigenius:core:description: Kinase-screening resource-allocation LP (worked example for the JuMP-HiGHS institution). A lab has 4 hours of plate-reader access and 6 hours of compound-handling capacity per shift. Each Kinase-Glo run consumes 1 plate-hour and 1 handling-hour and yields 3 information-units; each ADP-Glo run consumes 1 plate-hour and 2 handling-hours and yields 5 information-units. Maximise total information output. (LP relaxation; in practice the run counts would also be constrained to integers — that's a MIP variant.) Solution: n_kg = 2, n_ag = 2, objective = 16. Mirrors the LP probe in api-survey.md so the example doubles as a regression check.
urn:eigenius:julia:jump:model_source:
function build_model(optimizer)
    m = JuMP.Model(optimizer)
    JuMP.set_silent(m)
    JuMP.@variable(m, n_kg >= 0)
    JuMP.@variable(m, n_ag >= 0)
    JuMP.@constraint(m, plate_hours, n_kg + n_ag <= 4)
    JuMP.@constraint(m, handling_hours, n_kg + 2 * n_ag <= 6)
    JuMP.@objective(m, Max, 3 * n_kg + 5 * n_ag)
    return m
end

urn:eigenius:core:description: The OPTIMAL outcome: n_kg = 2, n_ag = 2, total information value = 16. Dual values report the marginal cost of each binding constraint (plate-hours and handling-hours both bind here). AutoOnLoad re-runs the LP via HiGHS and confirms.
